items.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
items.summary: Cisco disclosed a critical flaw in the AMP feature of Secure Email Gateway allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to write files and run commands as root; Cisco PSIRT confirms active exploitation. CERT-EU urges immediate patching.

items.title: 2026-016: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab CE and EE
items.summary: GitLab CE/EE releases 19.4.2, 19.3.4 and 19.2.8 fix 24 issues, including a critical unauthenticated remote code execution flaw. CERT-EU recommends prioritising internet-facing self-managed instances.

items.title: Hackers breach Microsoft 365 tenants via ConnectWise supply-chain attack
items.summary: ConnectWise shut down access to its Cloud Backup (ex-SkyKick) service after attackers abused application identities to compromise customer Microsoft 365 tenants — a supply-chain risk for MSP-served organisations.

items.title: Hackers Use Compromised ConnectWise Credential to Sign In to 173 Microsoft 365 Tenants
items.summary: Threat actors used a compromised Microsoft 365 credential tied to ConnectWise Cloud Backup to sign in to 173 customer M365 tenants; MSP-managed environments should review sign-in and consent logs.

items.title: 2026-015: Critical Vulnerability in Multiple Atlassian Products
items.summary: Atlassian patched a critical arbitrary file access vulnerability affecting Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible and Fisheye Data Center products. CERT-EU advises upgrading and reviewing access logs for exploitation signs.

items.title: Romanian F-16s shoot down two drones over Black Sea, authorities say
items.summary: Romanian F-16s on air policing duty shot down two jet-powered Geran-family attack drones over the Black Sea, per the Defence Ministry.

items.title: Drupal patches critical RCE flaws, warns exploits may emerge soon
items.summary: Drupal patched two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities affecting all supported versions and warned that exploits may appear soon.

items.title: MALFEX npm Package 'imgdecode' Hides Shellcode Loader in Windows Native Addon
items.summary: A malicious npm package 'imgdecode', part of the MALFEX supply-chain campaign, hides a shellcode loader in a Windows native addon; it had ~979 downloads and remained available on npm.

items.title: Israeli Ad Firm Doubled as Candiru’s Zero-Click Spyware Delivery Channel
items.summary: Researchers report Israeli ad firm Discover-Tech's advertising infrastructure was used as a delivery channel for Candiru zero-click spyware, enabling mass device fingerprinting and targeted infection.

items.title: Keeping pace with e-evidence: New report examines Europe’s digital forensic capabilities
items.summary: A European Commission/Europol report finds digital forensic tools, resources and expertise across the EU are struggling to keep pace with the volume and variety of modern e-evidence.

items.title: Iran says two tankers catch fire after hitting mines in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran says two crude oil tankers caught fire after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz, with the IRGC claiming they used an unauthorised route.

items.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
items.summary: The US president temporarily waived several recently legislated Russia sanctions citing national security, amid an escalating row with Ukraine's president.

items.title: Violent clashes, looting and buildings ablaze in France as over 1,000 arrested after protests
items.summary: More than 1,000 people were arrested in France after cost-of-living protests involving over half a million participants turned into looting and arson in several cities.

items.title: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine a ‘planned operation’, Zelenskyy says
items.summary: Ukraine's president claims Starlink speed restrictions in Ukraine were a planned operation, saying tests showed no such limits elsewhere in Europe — raising satellite connectivity dependency questions.

items.title: Cybercrims go beyond stealing data to attack physical building systems
items.summary: The Register reports cybercriminals increasingly moving beyond data theft to attack physical building systems, such as access control, affecting office operations.

items.title: Federal agencies recommend cyber controls, independent testing for frontier AI systems
items.summary: US federal agencies issued voluntary but detailed guidance recommending cybersecurity controls and independent testing for frontier AI systems, including securing sandbox environments during model testing.

items.title: Almost 50 arrested as police target Western Balkan network linked to killings
items.summary: Europol reports nearly 50 arrests in an international operation against a Western Balkan drug trafficking network linked to killings, kidnappings and grenade attacks across Europe.

items.title: Deaths, injuries after fire at Alberta military base: Canada minister
items.summary: Canada's defence minister confirms deaths and injuries after a fire at a military base in Alberta; cause and figures not yet disclosed.

items.title: St Petersburg under attack from Ukrainian drone swarm
items.summary: Multiple explosions reported in St Petersburg after a suspected Ukrainian drone swarm attack.

items.title: Rubio says Trump to take up to 60 days to weigh Russia sanctions
items.summary: Rubio says the US president will take up to 60 days to decide on Russia sanctions measures.

items.title: Buildings burn as French protests go into the night
items.summary: During nightly unrest in France, masked protesters set fire to Limoges town hall, which officials say is largely destroyed.

items.title: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats in the occupied West Bank
items.summary: Masked Israeli settlers attacked European diplomats, a French mayor and Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

items.title: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
items.summary: European diplomats were attacked by Israeli settlers in the West Bank; the Israeli military condemned the violence while the PM's office called it part of a smear campaign.

items.title: Student protests widen into greater social unrest in France
items.summary: Student protests in France widened into broader social unrest, with hundreds of demonstrations nationwide and some turning violent.

items.title: Historic Limoges town hall engulfed in flames amid protests in France
items.summary: The 143-year-old Limoges town hall was set ablaze during nationwide French cost-of-living protests.

items.title: Anti-government protesters battle with police in Albania
items.summary: Violent clashes between anti-government demonstrators and riot police continued in Tirana, Albania.

items.title: 'No room for violence,' says Macron after rioters and looters hijack peaceful demonstrations across France
items.summary: President Macron pledged accountability for rioters and looters who hijacked peaceful demonstrations across France, as the PM highlighted the cost of the damage.

items.title: Albanian police fire rubber bullets and arrest hundreds as anti-government protests enter fifth day
items.summary: Albanian police used rubber bullets and tear gas and made hundreds of arrests as anti-government protests entered a fifth day.

items.title: Protesters clash with police in Belgium as demonstrations turn violent across Europe
items.summary: Protests turned violent in Belgium, with the interior minister describing the situation as beyond simple protest, as unrest spreads across Europe.

items.title: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers amid rising violence in occupied West Bank
items.summary: Belgium's foreign minister blamed Israeli settlement policy for an attack on European diplomats in the West Bank and pledged to push for further EU sanctions.

items.title: AI rapidly improving, could vastly boost US GDP, Anthropic's Clark tells policymakers
items.summary: Anthropic's Jack Clark told US policymakers that AI capabilities are improving rapidly and could substantially boost GDP.

items.title: France's fridges hacked - when cyberattacks hit home
items.summary: Reuters report on cyberattacks reaching consumer devices in France, including hacked fridges, highlighting IoT exposure in homes.

items.title: No money for Ukraine and EU budget cuts: What could a Le Pen victory mean for the EU?
items.summary: Analysis of how a Le Pen victory in France's 2027 presidential election could mean EU budget cuts and no funding for Ukraine, setting Paris against Brussels.
